parsed.why: Birth-sex facility statute covering restrooms, shelters, dorms and prisons, religious-refusal service denials with immunity, no statewide non-discrimination; ranked in worst-law tier though no arrests or criminal penalties documented under it.

Criminalised birth-sex restroom use reaching private businesses — gas stations, restaurants, hospitals — with up to a year jail; only such law extending to private premises, making facility access an inescapable criminal exposure for any outed visitor.

State-level protections operate (public-accommodations law, hate-crime enhancements, shield laws, X markers), but the shared national regime — passport marker refusal, entry screening, federal facility bans and custody conversion-therapy policy — still binds every visitor here.

Veto-overridden law restricting public buildings including airports, with civil and criminal penalties plus private bounty lawsuits, and invalidated IDs; an independent assessment moved it to Do Not Travel for interstate visitors, with litigation unresolved.

Most-protective tier with goods-and-services non-discrimination, gender-identity hate-crime law, identity-consistent custody and strip-search policy, and a visitor-relevant care shield; only the parent's border document regime and federal exposures hold it below reduced-risk.
